kind: sign resolution for the structure -> behavior block
subject: docs/STRUCTURE-BEHAVIOR-DESIGN.md §6; synthetic worlds; no engine run, no seed
question: at n worlds per configuration, how often does this block's decision rule recover the relation with the correct sign, for a relation of size rho?
decision_rule_simulated: Spearman rank correlation across worlds; interval by resampling worlds; resolved only when the interval excludes zero with the predicted sign

reference_rule.name: smallest relation of interest
reference_rule.why: the bar is set at the weakest relation the design would call predictive. Setting it at a guessed effect size would make the answer depend on a number no artifact supplies; setting it at the smallest effect worth detecting makes the block's size a consequence of the claim instead of the claim a consequence of the size.

bootstrap_validation.note: the analytic column is Fisher's z on Spearman's r; the simulated column applies the protocol's bootstrap. They are two different interval constructions, so the difference is a check that the closed form is not doing the work alone, not an error estimate of either.

verdict.reading: at a true rank relation of 0.50, a block of 48 worlds per configuration resolves the sign with probability 0.902 at the 0.90 bar. Smaller blocks resolve only larger relations.

limits: The worlds are synthetic. This measures the estimator, not the size of the real relation.

Attenuation from DI's own measurement error is not modelled, so the computed probability is an upper bound on the real one. A noisy predictor shrinks the observed rank correlation before the interval is built.

The Gaussian copula assumes worlds are exchangeable draws. If configurations cluster as §5 suggests, the effective number of independent worlds is smaller than n and the probability is again an upper bound.
Only the primary configuration's rule is simulated. A secondary configuration with its own withheld set has its own outcome distribution and no number is transferred to it.
The 98.33 % level and the 0.90 bar are conventions. The artifact reports the grid so a different bar can be read off without recomputation.
